Worst Roads in SA

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
You nominate them... we drive them... looking for the Worst Roads in SA!

Unique Selling Point:
Potholes, washed away tar, non-existent road markings... we all know of that ONE road in SA that is supposedly the worst! So, let's get viewers to document their travels this Easter and nominate a road, that they believe is the worst in SA... Then we go out with a rigged vehicle and drive a few of the so-called worst roads in SA. Not a scientific study, just a fun way to highlight one of our biggest gripes in the country today.

Summary:
The idea came when I was driving on the 47km road between Vivo and Alldays in Limpopo... The road is bad. At times cars drive on the gravel shoulder of the road to avoid the potholes. At times the tar is completely washed away. Even large mining trucks drive like they are in a video game, zig-zagging across the road. What is more... there's hardly any cellphone signal... If you get stuck... you have to rely on a good Samaritan.

So, the idea is to take a few of the worst roads and drive them, and evaluate them according to a list of criteria... And at the end, we approach SANRAL/Govt and ask them... why is this the current state of our roads?

Further information:
Evaluating the roads:
30 to 50km provincial road
When driving we take a long an "assistant/researcher" who counts the potholes.... We get out and measure the big ones, test the cellphone signal, test passers-by's willingness to assist... Evaluate signage and road markings...
it can all be displayed visually like a score sheet...

The presenter and researcher will be driving a Toyota corolla (or similar) rigged with cameras... inside and out.... and a support vehicle will follow, also filming from behind...

But it's not all fun and games... we will approach the authorities in every case... to find out WHY the road is in this state and WHAT (if anything) is being done...

** I propose that we ask viewers to be on the lookout for "bad roads" over Easter, and then send us cellphone videos or photos, and locations of proposed roads... Then we pick 3 or so (depending on feasibility and budget) and go and drive them....

Press Release:


Pitiful Potholes
Coffee Bay on the Wild Coast is one of the most pristine locations in South Africa. Home to a tourist favourite - the Hole in the Wall - also affectionately known as “izi Khaleni” or “the place of thunder”, it should be teeming with visitors. But few are brave enough to tackle the treacherous pothole ridden 75km stretch of tarred road intended to get you there. It’s just one example of the shocking state of most roads around the country. Winding gauntlets full of deep ditches and craters that have been left unattended for so long, that there is often more pothole than road left to drive on. It’s a symptom of the rampant mismanagement plaguing municipalities. The general malaise of poor service delivery in most communities. On a road trip to nowhere, Carte Blanche drove through just three provinces to find some of the country’s worst roads. And what we found, was disturbing.

WORST ROADS IN SA
VIEWER CLIPS

Driving in South Africa is a lot… traffic, exacerbated by loadshedding… impatient motorists, taxis, buses, trucks… and potholes!

She and her husband were travelling on the R36, on their way to the Kruger National Park…

I mean this makes me a little vulnerable to tell you because I try not to be a fearful person. But I said to Spense… let’s turn around and go home… this is much too nerve-wracking.
V/O
Her tweet hit a cord with many South Africans – and people started sharing similar experiences across the country..
Ferial
That was my most viral tweet ever. I literally got hundreds and hundreds of responses. So I started collating them and seeing if they’re telling you a story… and then I realised, actually it’s a national story… Our whole road network is like that.
V/O
And that is what set us off on our mission… to drive - what are considered - some of the worst roads in South Africa…
We asked you, our viewers, to nominate potential candidates, and in the end we settled on 4 regions… in 4 different provinces…
V/O
First Up… We headed to Mpumalanga in search of the now infamous R36…
LINK
Hello?

Okay, for this official unofficial experiment to work we’ve set up a camera on the bonnet. We have another camera inside the cab. You, Kobus, will be sitting on the back seat with a camera and I also have my trusty assistant. Could you please explain to us how is this gonna work?

Assistant: Yes, this is my road danger-o-meter. It’s broken up into seven parameters – those being general road state, damage to the vehicle, road paint and signage….

What he’s trying to say is we’re going to drive this road and just see the state of it…

Trusty assistant!
UPSOUND
Let’s go!

Claire: The road is looking not too bad…

Assistant: The paint’s little faded but…

Claire: You are paying attention to a lot of details….


V/O
Within the first few kilometres we count around 80 potholes… many have been filled with sand…

The uneven road surface doesn’t seem to deter the large trucks barreling down the road…
UPSOUND
Oh Gosh
V/O
The good news for future users… further South, there is major construction on the road … but right now, that doesn’t make driving it any easier.
UPSOUND
Do you know what I used to make fun of people living in cities driving off road vehicles, t… now I realise you actually need an off road vehicle to drive a provincial road!
V/O
But if it were just the one bad road, drivers could try and avoid it… sadly all the provincial roads in the area are dotted with deep menacing potholes…
Kgatlego
One of the worst 5 i have to drive – hikjacking accident




V/O
This is Mashishing. It used to be called Lydenburg which means “place of suffering” … looking at the roads, they should’ve perhaps kept the name…
SPIROS
You don't want to drive on roads that are shocking like this.
Oh. My goodness.


V/O
Spiros Couvaras is a driving instructor – and local ward councillor – here in town... He knows these roads like the back of his hand.
Spiros
You know, they don't pay me to push cars, cause if we get stuck.
On, we're not going to push the cart and worry about it. Now, it's not my intention to get stuck.
V/O
And of course it wasn’t our intention to get stuck either, but this road to a local school for children with disabilities… got the better of our production vehicle and some on-site emergency surgery was needed when the front bash plate got damaged…
V/O
The collapse of road infrastructure has had a ripple effect on this community…
UPSOUND
This is unbelievable, Spiros!
Spiros
A lot of big companies have left town because of this poor management system of theirs, and this lack of interest is lack of empathy and.
00:27:26:14 - 00:27:28:10
Speaker 3
Readiness about how.
00:27:29:02 - 00:27:32:10
Speaker 1
Like this really this is not the way to do it.


V/O
To better understand the overall state of our roads, we contacted SAICE – the South African Institution of Civil Engineering, which published its fourth Report Card on Infrastructure in December 2022.
V/O
Friedrich Slabbert serves on its Board. And as the former chairperson of the Transport Division he was responsible for collating the information used to compile the most recent Infrastructure report card..
Friedrich Slabbert
One must realize that the roads aspects are varying from national roads, provincial roads, metropolitan roads, and then you have the lower level of district roads.


V/O
South Africa has a road network of about 750 000 kilometres… with by far the majority – 80% – of our roads being gravel. But they are by no means less important..
Friedrich Slabbert
How do farmers get the products produced to the market?
00:04:21:20 - 00:04:50:05
Speaker 1
So if those roads are not in a good condition, then it has an economic impact on those people. But it also is a situation in terms of the social impact.
V/O
Across the country people rely on roads to get to schools, clinics, churches.. And of course their jobs… Bad roads affect everybody.
Jack Armour
Farmer that are, that have got trucks and lorries, that are trying to supply goods to the market, their expenses have increased dramatically because of the poor roads.
V/O
Dr Jack Armour is the operations manager at Free State Agriculture.


A lot of agricultural companies refuse to make deliveries to the farm anymore, so now the farmer has to use his own transport to go fetch those products.


LINK
The Free State is notorious for bad roads, In fact, Macfarlane was here just less than a year ago reporting on the worst roads and the provincial government’s promises to fix them. But looking at the state of this provincial road that is supposed to be tarred… I guess they’ve been busy doing other things?
Jack Armour
There are some roads where you've got to slow down to literally 5, 10 kilometers an hour and you've got to wait for oncoming traffic to try and navigate a piece of the road that is passable.
UPSOUND
Now we’re in the beautiful Free State, driving from Marquard to Clocolan because we’ve heard… wow… that the roads are particularly bad here, littered with potholes and that truck just scared me…
V/O
Once again we are surprised by the amount of heavy traffic on what is a rather narrow road…
Jack Armour
The Free State is the central province in South Africa. So everybody transverses through the Free State and one of the big culprits is manganese trucks. So the mining in the Northern Cape, these big trucks go through the southern Free State to some of the main roads in the central free state, to the ports in Richards Bay and PE and mess up our roads.
V/O
The near collapse of our rail system hasn’t helped matters…
Friedrich Slabbert
Traffic per say is not the cause. We designed roads and we estimate through growth rates and current traffic counts, we estimate over the next 20 years what the loading will be. So, that we designed for but for overloading, you have no estimate for that. Also, you cannot design for illegal use…
V/O
So trucks using roads not geared for heavy loads, or even overloading trucks… are having a huge impact on our roads…
Jack Armour
Law enforcement is supposed to be on the roads with Weighbridge is making sure that trucks aren't overloaded. That's another huge issue. So we’re stuck now with this road freight issue that is totally overloading our roads.
UPSOUND
Look at that.. On the side. Look how deep that is.
Jeez!
That is Shocking….
Should I get a shot?
Ja,
I think so…
V/O
Potholes are not just a hazard for vehicles!


Assistant slipping
V/O
While our Provincial road network is “not coping” and “at risk of failure”, our municipal or regional roads are generally in an even worse state…
LINK
Almost half of all our roads are managed by municipalities… and if you look at the legacy of municipal governance over the past few decades….. It's no surprise that our roads too are “falling apart”...
V/O
Station street in Clocolan is a minefield…
UPSOUND
Have you long given up counting how many potholes are on this road?
Cause there’s all the ones we’re going through and then there’s all the ones we’re not going through…
I’m trying to miss them, but you have to choose the lesser of the pothole…Right now Clocolan leading in the Pothole Olympics
V/O
But believe it or not… this is not the worst road we’ve encountered…
LINK
For the North West leg of our not-so-scientific study, we took to social media to ask you, our viewers which is the worst roads… the answer… was pick one.. Any one… so here I am on the R53 between Swartruggens and Ventersdorp… and let me tell you so far, so very, very bad…
V/O
Trusty Assistant counted over 400 potholes within a few kilometres… but couldn’t keep up!
UPSOUND
For this I have just written A LOT in all caps…
Very scientific and accurate…
V/O
And some of these potholes are MASSIVE
UPSOUND
That’s about 2 metres…
WHAT?
V/O
But how does a road end up looking like this?
The short answer is … 66 different road authorities in South Africa, and no single overarching governing body.
Friedrich Slabbert
The smaller towns, Rustenburg or Lydenburg, Koster… any of those smaller towns.. They have about the same number of kilometres of road than the provinces.
So now immediately brings us to skills. How how do we. Do we have the same types of of skills available at the district level compared to a province?
V/O
SAICE’s report card shows a dramatic decline in experienced professional engineers – indicated in red – working in local government … and this is apparent in many of our current road management systems … once a pothole appears.. It’s actually already too late.
Friedrich Slabbert
If we do preventative maintenance, a certain action will cost one, right? If we delayed by one or two years, that same car cost will be addressed. And if we delayed by another two or three years, that cost will be 16.
V/O
Right now we need an estimated R500 billion to fix our roads. Money we don’t have.
UPSOUND
73
73 Potholes on this road that we’ve been driving.
Yes.
I would never have guessed… I thought it was much less than that.This just shows I’m becoming immune to sighting potholes….
V/O
After 5 days on the road, and having driven almost 3000 kms… we’re back where we started… in the leafy suburbs of Johannesburg where the roads sadly tell the same story….
Ferial
With over 40,000 potholes in Johannesburg, that does tell you that you're getting to the end of your usable road network.

Claire: But what would you say to somebody? I mean, what are potholes a symptom of?

Potholes are a symptom of corruption. They are a symptom of an absence of maintenance, and they're a symptom and a symbol of a government that simply doesn't care anymore.


















PROMO 1 11”
5 days, 4 provinces, and almost 3000 kilometres … in search of POTHOLES!
UPSOUND – That’s about 2 metres!
WHAT?


PROMO 2 21”
UPSOUND: You know driving in the countryside is supposed to be relaxing… It’s supposed to ease stress. You’re supposed to enjoy nature… Instead I’m focussing on the roads because of the potholes!
VO:
On a road trip to nowhere, we go searching for some of South Africa’s worst roads.
PROMO 3 21”
Potholes and dongas are mushrooming all over the country…
UPSOUND: at some point you have to actually get off the road and travel on the side of the road
We went on a road trip to find some of South Africa’s worst roads!
UPSOUND: I am trying to miss them, but you have to choose the lesser of the pothole

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): You nominate them... we drive them... looking for the Worst Roads in SA!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Potholes, washed away tar, non-existent road markings... we all know of that ONE road in SA that is supposedly the worst! So, let's get viewers to document their travels this Easter and nominate a road, that they believe is the worst in SA... Then we go out with a rigged vehicle and drive a few of the so-called worst roads in SA. Not a scientific study, just a fun way to highlight one of our biggest gripes in the country today.
metadata.Summary: The idea came when I was driving on the 47km road between Vivo and Alldays in Limpopo... The road is bad. At times cars drive on the gravel shoulder of the road to avoid the potholes. At times the tar is completely washed away. Even large mining trucks drive like they are in a video game, zig-zagging across the road. What is more... there's hardly any cellphone signal... If you get stuck... you have to rely on a good Samaritan. So, the idea is to take a few of the worst roads and drive them, and evaluate them according to a list of criteria... And at the end, we approach SANRAL/Govt and ask them... why is this the current state of our roads?
metadata.Further information: Evaluating the roads: 30 to 50km provincial road When driving we take a long an "assistant/researcher" who counts the potholes.... We get out and measure the big ones, test the cellphone signal, test passers-by's willingness to assist... Evaluate signage and road markings... it can all be displayed visually like a score sheet... The presenter and researcher will be driving a Toyota corolla (or similar) rigged with cameras... inside and out.... and a support vehicle will follow, also filming from behind... But it's not all fun and games... we will approach the authorities in every case... to find out WHY the road is in this state and WHAT (if anything) is being done... ** I propose that we ask viewers to be on the lookout for "bad roads" over Easter, and then send us cellphone videos or photos, and locations of proposed roads... Then we pick 3 or so (depending on feasibility and budget) and go and drive them....
